title: Mr Kim Calls Me Professor
mood: a nickname that turned out to be a prophecy
subject: a corner store owner who nicknamed a twelve-year-old Professor
caption: Baltimore club rap. The classic Baltimore club kick pattern with its syncopated boom-boom-bap feel, a looped Think break underneath, short shouted chant samples answering the rapper, layered hand claps, a simple stabbed synth bass. Raw and loud with the kicks forward and almost no reverb, deliberately rough rather than polished. Male rap voice with his cadence locked tightly to the eighth-note grid, conversational and proud, with call-and-response chants on the hook. 130 BPM, G minor. A nickname that turned out to be a prophecy. No trap hi-hat rolls, no Jersey club bed squeak, no sung pop chorus, no autotune, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - Baltimore club kicks and Think break]

[Verse 1]
Corner store on Greenmount, Mr Kim behind the glass
Calls everybody something, never once your name
Big Man, Sneakers, Little Sister, Doctor, Boss
Me he calls Professor 'cause I read the cereal box

[Hook]
Mr Kim calls me Professor
Twelve years old, I didn't earn it, now I'm thirty and I'm trying
Every time I walk in he says it like it's true
And I stand up straighter every single time

[Verse 2]
Told him last week I finally finished the degree
Night school, six years, nobody threw me a thing
He came round the counter, which he never does
Shook my hand and gave me a soda and wouldn't let me pay

[Hook]
Mr Kim calls me Professor
Twelve years old, I didn't earn it, now I'm thirty and I earned it
Every time I walk in he says it like it's true
And now it is, and he was first

[Outro - chant and kicks]
Professor. Professor.
Green soda. On the house.
